candidates.title: [Bug]: xml template with interpolation produces a read-only value
candidates.body:
### Description An xml template expression containing any interpolation (in content or in an attribute) constructs a read-only xml value. `x is readonly` is `true` and mutating it (`setName`, `setChildren`, writing to the attribute map) panics with `cannot mutate readonly XML element`. The same template without interpolation (`xml `

``) is correctly mutable. Interpolating a mutable xml value (`xml `

${c}

``) also yields a read-only result. ### Steps to Reproduce ```ballerina import ballerina/io; public function main() { string s = "v"; xml x = xml `

${s}

`; io:println(x is readonly); // @output false if x is xml:Element { x.setName("q"); map attrs = x.getAttributes(); attrs["b"] = "w"; x.setChildren("new"); io:println(x); // @output new } } ``` Run with `go run ./cli/cmd run .bal`. **Actual:** ``` true error: cannot mutate readonly XML element at main(template-interp-mutable-v.bal:8) ``` **Expected:** ``` false new ``` **Spec reasoning:** - §6.6.2 (XML template expression): evaluation makes "a new copy ... of the xml value and the result of the expression evaluations are inserted". The only rule that sets the read-only bit is: "An xml-template-expr occurring within a const-expr will construct an xml value that has its read-only bit on." - §5.3.2: only `xml:Text` and the empty xml value are inherently immutable; elements, PIs and comments are selectively immutable, so a template element outside a const-expr must be mutable. Note: `corpus/bal/subset10/10-xml-navigation/lang-xml-errors-v.bal` (around lines 206–231) relies on this behaviour, using an empty `${emptyInsertion}` interpolation to obtain a read-only element; that fixture would need another way to get a read-only value. ### Affected Version(s) nutcracker `main` @ 8d7d45394 ### OS, DB, other environment details and versions Linux, Go toolchain from the repo's go.mod ### Related area Runtime ### Related issue(s) (optional) Possibly related: #1628 (template isolation analysis; different issue).

[Bug]: error constructor accepts a non-definite contextually expected type
candidates.body:
### Description
An error constructor without an error-type-reference is accepted when the applicable contextually expected type is a union of distinct error types (not definite). The constructed value belongs to neither member of its static type, breaking type soundness. `DA|error q = error("u");` is accepted the same way and `q is DA` is false (here the plain-`error` member could arguably be selected, but the union is still not definite).

### Steps to Reproduce
```ballerina
import ballerina/io;

type DA distinct error;
type DB distinct error;

public function main() {
    DA|DB u = error("u"); // @error
    io:println(u is DA || u is DB);
}
```
Run with `go run ./cli/cmd run <file>.bal`.

**Actual:**
```
(no diagnostic; program runs and prints)
false
```
**Expected:**
```
a compile error on the marked line (contextually expected type for error constructor must be definite)
```

**Spec reasoning:**
- §6.17 (Error constructor): "The applicable contextually expected type E must be definite."
- §5.7.7: "A union type T1|T2 is definite if and only if both T1 and T2 are definite and the set of type-ids induced by T1 and T2 are the same." `DA` and `DB` are distinct and induce different type-ids, so `DA|DB` is not definite.
- §5.1: "The set of type-ids of an object or error value are those induced by the type-descriptor used to construct it; such a type descriptor must therefore be definite."
- nutcracker builds a value whose static type is `DA|DB` but for which both `u is DA` and `u is DB` are false.

### Affected Version(s)
nutcracker `main` @ 8d7d45394

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions
Linux, Go toolchain from the repo's go.mod

### Related area
Type checker

### Related issue(s) (optional)
Supporting: #1375 (closed, not planned) — `distinct (A|B)` rejected because a union of distinct error types is not definite; the same rule applies here.
